task_description: CLI permissions snapshot integration testing - Implement a mechanism to record IAM roles assumed and actions performed during CLI integration tests, storing them as snapshots that fail tests when changed

features.description: Create AWS SDK v3 permissions recording middleware that intercepts and records all IAM roles assumed and actions performed during SDK calls
steps: Create new package 'tools/@aws-cdk/permissions-recorder' with package.json, tsconfig.json, and standard CDK tooling setup
Implement PermissionsRecorder class with start(), stop(), getRecordedPermissions(), and reset() methods
Create AWS SDK v3 middleware plugin that hooks into the middleware stack at the 'initialize' step
Intercept all SDK requests to extract: service name (from clientName), action name (from Command name), and region
Special handling for STS service: capture AssumeRole/AssumeRoleWithSAML/AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity calls and extract RoleArn from input parameters
Implement PermissionsSnapshot interface with structure: { roles: string[], actions: { service: string, action: string, count: number }[] }
Add helper method to apply middleware to any AWS SDK v3 client instance
Write comprehensive unit tests for middleware interception, role capture, and action recording
acceptance_criteria: Middleware successfully intercepts all AWS SDK v3 service calls without affecting functionality
STS AssumeRole calls are captured with the target role ARN
All service:action combinations are recorded with call counts
Recorder can be started, stopped, and reset cleanly

features.description: Integrate permissions recorder into integration test execution workflow and write permissions snapshot files
steps: Modify 'tools/@aws-cdk/integration-test-deployment/lib/integration-test-runner.ts' to import and initialize PermissionsRecorder
Start recording before each integration test batch execution in deployIntegrationTest()
Create helper function to inject middleware into CDK CLI's AWS SDK clients (via environment variable or SDK configuration)
After test execution, retrieve recorded permissions and write to snapshot directory
Implement permissions snapshot file format: '<test-name>.permissions.snapshot.json' stored in the test's .snapshot/ directory
Ensure snapshot file is sorted deterministically (roles alphabetically, actions by service then action name)
Add configuration option to enable/disable permissions recording (default: enabled)
Handle errors gracefully - permissions recording failure should not fail the test
Update integration-test-deployment package.json to add dependency on permissions-recorder
acceptance_criteria: Permissions snapshot file is generated for each integration test run
Snapshot file contains all IAM roles assumed during test
Snapshot file contains all service:action combinations with counts
Snapshot file format is deterministic and diff-friendly (sorted, formatted JSON)
Recording can be disabled via configuration
Test execution completes successfully with recording enabled

features.description: Implement snapshot comparison logic and clear failure reporting when permissions change
steps: Create PermissionsSnapshotComparator class in permissions-recorder package
Implement comparison logic: detect added roles, removed roles, added actions, removed actions, changed action counts
Generate structured diff output: { addedRoles: [], removedRoles: [], addedActions: [], removedActions: [], changedCounts: [] }
Integrate comparison into integ-runner workflow: after test, compare generated snapshot with existing snapshot
If no existing snapshot exists, write new snapshot and pass (first run behavior)
If snapshot differs, fail the test with detailed diff output showing exactly what changed
Add --update-permissions-snapshot flag to integ-runner to update snapshots when changes are intentional
Format diff output for GitHub Actions visibility (use ::error:: and ::warning:: syntax)
Add documentation to INTEGRATION_TESTS.md explaining the permissions snapshot feature
Write integration tests that verify the snapshot comparison and failure behavior
acceptance_criteria: Tests fail with clear error message when permissions snapshot changes unexpectedly
Diff output clearly shows added/removed roles and actions
New tests automatically create baseline permissions snapshot
Users can update snapshots intentionally with --update-permissions-snapshot flag
GitHub Actions output is properly formatted for visibility
Documentation explains the feature and how to handle snapshot updates
